candidates.name: Strict Safety
candidates.principle: Single-scenario safety first. Any regression versus LOCAL is a deployment defect.

rationale.C1: Zero allowed degrade rate: a planner change must not make any scenario worse than LOCAL.
rationale.C2: Zero allowed worst-case ΔR: the worst scenario must stay non-negative versus LOCAL.
rationale.C3: Mean ΔR >= 0 is implied by strict non-inferiority; recorded explicitly as a floor of 0.
rationale.C4: Mean U_traj must not fall below LOCAL. No positive bit-margin is invented from current gain.
rationale.C5: forbid_all: fallback to LOCAL is not an excuse to accept a harmful B2 substitution.
rationale.C6: strict non-inferiority: for every scenario, R_selected >= R_LOCAL.
rationale.C7: A second unseen batch is required before a strict-safety claim can be treated as deployable.
rationale.C8: One additional independently generated batch beyond 220000-220063.

candidates.name: Balanced Deployment
candidates.principle: Allow only rare, bounded losses; require non-negative average gain and one extra unseen batch.

rationale.C1: 1-in-100 rare-event cap. Decimal 0.01 is a conventional reliability quota, not 3/64 or 0.047.
rationale.C2: At most 0.10 of the R unit interval [0, 1]. A one-tenth score drop is the design loss bound, not -0.214.
rationale.C3: Average rank-normalized score must not decline. Floor is 0, not 0.111.
rationale.C4: Average payload must not decline versus LOCAL. Floor is 0 bits, not the current 1.34e6 gain.
rationale.C5: A rare degradation is allowed only if it also respects the C2 loss bound.
rationale.C6: aggregate non-inferiority: summary statistics may pass even if a rare scenario does not.
rationale.C7: One new unseen batch is required so Gate-1 safety is not judged only on 220000-220063.

candidates.name: Conservative-with-Fallback
candidates.principle: Use LOCAL fallback as a risk control; allow limited degradation if average gain, bounded loss, and repeated unseen batches all hold.

rationale.C1: 2-in-100 limited-tolerance cap. Decimal 0.02 is a conventional minority quota, not 3/64.
rationale.C2: At most 1/8 of the R unit interval. Dyadic 0.125 is a design constant, not a pad around -0.214.
rationale.C3: At least 0.02 of the R unit interval as a minimum average improvement that can justify changing planner defaults.
rationale.C4: Average payload must still not fall below LOCAL. No bit-margin is copied from current U gain.
rationale.C5: allow_some: fallback already withholds B2 when margin < tau; residual degradations are tolerated only inside C1/C2.
rationale.C6: aggregate non-inferiority; strict per-scenario non-inferiority is not required because fallback is part of the system.
rationale.C7: Independent hold-out is mandatory for this candidate by design.
rationale.C8: Two additional independently generated batches, because fallback-plus-B2 is a system claim, not a single-table claim.

gate_vs_criterion.Gate-1: Per-scenario switch: use B2 iff score margin >= frozen tau. Does not decide planner integration.
gate_vs_criterion.deployment_criterion: System-level acceptance of frozen B2 + frozen Gate-1. Does not change the per-scenario switch.

frozen_gate.rule: if margin >= tau: B2 else LOCAL
